items.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I just finished, as I said, last night I went down and did a set with Terry Gibbs and Buddy DeFranco down at the other hotel.

ctx.x: That must be a great feeling — to drive a big band — I would think.

Yeah. I enjoy it very much. I love working with my band, but I love working with a lot of other bands, as you just mentioned, this weekend is pretty busy with me. And tomorrow I’m going to be down at the Marriott where there’s another jazz party going on with Terry Gibbs Dream Band. And then tonight I’m going up to Santa Barbara to do a © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

concert with Supersax. Now Med Flory has added a brass section to Supersax, and four voices. So it’s now the L.A. Voices he calls it. Sue Raney is the lead singer and the brass section, so it’s kind of, what do you call it, Supersax with voices? Or, I don’t know, it doesn’t matter what it’s called, it’s still big band and it’s fun to do. I like all kinds of playing. I enjoy doing what we’re doing here at this and I’m playing, I just finished, as I said, last night I went down and did a set with Terry Gibbs and…

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I took Frank Capp on drums, my drummer

ctx.x: And I admire that and so I wanted to talk about your TV band days. I’m imagining that that was a pressure situation. Like, okay Terry, tomorrow we’ve got this certain guest and they want this theme, and have it ready. Is that correct?

Well I’ll tell you how it all started. I used to be — Steve Allen was my friend. I was friends with Steve in the early 40s, late 40s. He became my friend then he became a big fan of mine, you know. And when he got his TV show he got me as a guest all the time, I was a guest a lot. And we were doing the show in California and I did his show with them and one of the producers, he loved me. He loved my dumb sense of humor, because I’m not a comedian but I’ve got the wit sort of like Steve’s. Steve loved me because,…

they said, “Okay we want you, it’s your job, but Steve Allen had a nine piece orchestra, we’ll give you a nine piece orchestra.” I said, “I don’t want it.” They said, “Well what do you mean?” I said, “You mean they give me a big band because we’re opposite Johnny Carson? Or opposite Elliot Lawrence who was with Les Crane — those shows at that time they all had 16 piece bands. And to me a 16 piece band — give me a sextet. I said sextet? Can you make it with a sextet? You see working with Steve Allen, of course I…

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: But there’s guys that have been working for me for thirty years now, when I put the band together. And so every once in a while, that cliché, when they make me an offer I can’t refuse. But now they’re all leaders by the way. Med Flory, Frank Capp.

ctx.x: She was and old time movie columnist who could make you or break you, you know, in the movie business. She’d be sitting there. It didn’t make any sense that people were coming to see the band. And we were the heroes. We played — $15 a night and our bar tabs were $23. You’ve got to be an idiot to do that. We were having so much fun. We didn’t care about the music. And that went on for about five weeks in a row. It was Mondays, maybe two nights a week. Then the club owner says, “Why don’t we do this five nights a…

tell you what I need now.” I’m the band leader, there was something I wanted to hear. You know, right or wrong, I wanted to hear something that I wanted. It started with, “You hear how the lead trumpet player, how you can hear him so well?” “Yeah.” I said, “Now let me hear the fourth trumpet player. All four trumpets. On the same level.” I wanted to hear the sound of a band, not protruding notes. Now great, now you hear? In the old days, by the way, it was hard to record the bass. All you heard was boom-boom-…
